Getting a Crown

A 1-minute patient guide with narration. Press space to pause.

Patient guide

Getting a crown.

Here is what to expect, start to finish.

Why a crown?

A crown covers a tooth that is cracked, worn down, or weakened by a large filling, so it can keep doing its job.

You'll be comfortable.

We numb the area first. You will feel pressure, but you should not feel pain.

A gentle reshape.

We remove a thin layer of the tooth so the crown has room to fit.

A precise scan.

A quick digital scan or impression captures the exact shape of your tooth and your bite.

Protected in the meantime.

A temporary crown covers the tooth while your permanent one is made. Some offices can make it the same day.

Then, the fit.

Your permanent crown is checked for fit, bite, and color before it is bonded in place.

Easy to care for.

Treat it like any other tooth.

Brush twice a dayFloss dailyKeep your checkups

Questions? Just ask.

Your dental team is happy to walk you through every step before, during, and after your visit.
